subject: Re: Adding capacity mid-term — commit top-up and throughput guardrails
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@acme.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity add — need mid-term top-up and throughput guarantees

Hi Dylan,

We're planning to increase our real-time inference footprint ahead of a major product launch in Q3. Current Dedicated pool is saturated during peak windows and the latency tail is starting to impact our user flows. We'd like to explore a mid-term top-up to our reserved commit (add ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs) and discuss throughput guardrails so we can hit 95th percentile p99 latency targets for 512-token sequences.

Key asks:
- Pricing for a 8-GPU mid-term top-up (monthly pricing + any pro-rated commit adjustments).
- What throughput guarantees you can commit to (tokens/sec per GPU or equivalent).
- How caching/batching will interact with our SLA and whether we can set a baseline throughput that triggers extra capacity automatically.

I've attached an internal traffic profile and requirements spreadsheet (ACME_requirements.xlsx). Sanjay (cc) will own the technical validation. Can we get a ballpark by EOD Fri?

Thanks —
Anna Li
Head of ML Platforms
Acme.ai

Attachment: ACME_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Anna Li <anna@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity add — need mid-term top-up and throughput guarantees

Anna — thanks for the context and the profile. High level answer first, details below. We can absolutely do a mid-term top-up and offer a measured throughput guarantee tied to a spike window and request mix. I'll run numbers with Marissa and Karthik and follow up with a concrete quote by Friday.

Options we'll propose (summary):
- Option A: 8-GPU top-up on a month-to-month add-on (no change to existing commit); higher per-GPU rate, immediate availability.
- Option B: Convert top-up into a stepped commit for the remainder of the 12-month term (pro-rated), better per-GPU economics and SLA inclusion.
- Option C: Temporary burst pool with auto-burst to spare capacity and a usage-based bill for overshoot (good if you expect short spikes).

Throughput guardrails: we suggest defining an operational SLO based on p99 latency for 512-token inference and a separate throughput baseline (tokens/sec) measured over 5-minute intervals. If baseline is breached for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows we trigger either auto-scaling (if enabled) or failover to a higher latency but lower-cost model variant — both options can be codified in the rollout policy. We can attach a credit schedule for SLA misses (tiered, capped).

Karthik — can you validate whether the sample traffic in the sheet will fit 8 A100-equiv GPUs at our recommended batching profile? Also, attach any perf-run artifacts we should share.

I'll include a draft quote in my next email.

—Dylan
Sr. Solutions Partner, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Anna Li <anna@acme.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed commit top-up quote and SLA framework (doc attached)

Anna / Dylan — attaching a formal quote and a short SLA addendum (proposed_commit_topup_quote.pdf). Summary below.

Summary of commercial proposal:
- Scenario 1 (Top-up, short term): +8 GPUs as a month-to-month top-up. Unit price: $6,750/GPU-month. No change to existing commit; 30-day minimum. No SLA credits for this option.
- Scenario 2 (Stepped commit): Convert +8 GPUs into a pro-rated step increase on the existing 12-month commitment. Effective unit price: $4,900/GPU-month (reflects commit discount). Requires formal amendment (DocuSign link below). Includes baseline throughput SLA and access to Dedicated support level.
- Scenario 3 (Burst policy): 4 dedicated GPUs + auto-burst to shared pool during spikes. Lower base cost but OTT charges for burst usage. Not recommended if you need strict tail latency control.

SLA highlights (applies to Scenario 2 only):
- Measured metric: p99 inference latency (512-token, production model) over 5-minute rolling windows.
- Guardrail: We guarantee p99 <= 600ms for baseline throughput up to 1.2M tokens/min across the committed pool.
- Remediation: Tiered credit schedule (5% credit for single missed 5-minute window, 2x credit for sustained miss >30 min, capped at 25% monthly).
- Measurement and validation: Redwood telemetry + customer-side sampling. Joint runbook for incident validation.

Discount / Commercial levers:
- We can extend a 6% additional discount if you sign the stepped commit within 10 business days and commit to a 12-month extension.
- One-time onboarding credit: we can offer $15k implementation credit for joint perf validation runs (limited-time).

Links / next steps:
- Quote PDF: proposed_commit_topup_quote.pdf (attached)
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

If this looks close, Dylan / Karthik can run the perf validation tomorrow and we can target a signed amendment next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_commit_topup_quote.pdf (PDF, 84KB)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Li <anna@acme.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed commit top-up quote and SLA framework (doc attached)

Thanks for the proposal. A few follow-ups from the engineering side: 

1) The p99 <= 600ms guardrail at 1.2M tokens/min looks promising, but we need clarity on how queuing is treated during short bursts. If requests queue at the load balancer, are they considered in the p99 calculation? We prefer credits only when Redwood-side processing contributes to the tail.

2) Can we get a soft SLA during the first 30 days of the stepped commit (monitor-only) before credits become active? We want to validate telemetry alignment.

3) Regarding the additional 6% discount tied to the commit window — can you confirm whether that stacks with our existing renewal discount (we currently have a 10% renewal loyalty discount)?

If we can get answers to 1–3 and a short perf run report (sample traces) after Karthik's validation, we should be able to route for procurement sign-off.

—Sanjay
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Acme.ai
